sources.title: Recovered interview note describing the counterclockwise-matrix coding prompt
Structured interview note containing the counterclockwise-matrix prompt
Tagged repository question record for counterclockwise matrix traversal
Deterministic Java validation against an independent direction/visited oracle

claims.text: The recovered source asks only to hand-write counterclockwise matrix printing; it does not state a starting corner or first movement direction, so the candidate explicitly fixes a top-left/downward contract before coding.
The exact Java implementation traverses a rectangular matrix with four shrinking boundaries in the declared counterclockwise order and rechecks boundary validity after each consumed edge.
The deterministic fixture compares the boundary-shrinking implementation with a structurally different per-cell direction/visited simulation for 3000 fixed-seed rectangular matrices.
The fixture covers null, zero-row, zero-column, single-row, single-column, 2x2, rectangular matrices in both orientations, and explicitly rejects ragged or null-row arrays.
For a rectangular matrix, each element is emitted once by the four-boundary implementation; aside from the returned output list, the implementation keeps only constant-size boundary state.

checks: declared top-left/down counterclockwise contract on fixed examples
3000 fixed-seed rectangles match independent direction/visited oracle
ragged and null-row inputs are rejected

boundary_tests.expected: every element is emitted exactly once in the declared traversal order
outer and inner layers follow the top-left/down counterclockwise contract without omission or duplication
IllegalArgumentException is thrown instead of indexing inconsistent row shapes
four-boundary output equals the independent direction/visited oracle

findings: The candidate treats the unspecified start corner as a source-boundary ambiguity rather than pretending counterclockwise alone determines one unique output sequence.
The chosen top-left/downward contract is stated before implementation and exercised by fixed examples.
Boundary rechecks address the core single-row/single-column duplicate-output failure mode.
The randomized oracle uses a direction/visited state machine rather than duplicating the four-boundary algorithm.
Rectangular-input and ragged-input behavior are explicit, so Java int[][] shape assumptions are not hidden.
No project metrics or production experience are invented.
Required human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
